note: Seeded from RESEARCH.md §5-6 (verified 2026-09-16). Edit in SignalPath → SETTINGS, not here.

anthem-mdx-16.notes: Digital ins are PCM-only (bitstream mutes) — pair sources with a 2ch downmix. No HDMI/eARC. AUDIT 2026-09-27: the 2 stereo line outs are hard-wired passthroughs of analog inputs 6 and 7 (live even in standby), not matrix outputs; the optical out repeats the selected digital input. Anthem's web spec omits the 2 coax inputs — the manual (§3.8) confirms 2 coax + 2 optical.

anthem-mdx-8.notes: No coax, no line outs, no digital out.

anthem-mrx-540-8k.notes: HDMI out 1 = eARC. AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 1 optical out + 1 line out; pre-outs 7.2. Anthem lists NO Zone 2 on the 540 (Zone 2 HDMI + zone-2 amp reassignment are 740/1140 only) — confirm before promising a second zone.

anthem-mrx-740-8k.notes: Zone-2 HDMI or amp-reassign. AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 1 optical out + 1 line out; pre-outs 11.2; third HDMI out is Zone-2 HDMI. Anthem's web spec lists the 740's two sub outs as PARALLEL (the 540/1140 are independent) — don't plan independent subs on a 740.

anthem-mrx-1140-8k.notes: AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 1 optical out + 1 line out; 15.2 processing with 2 independent subs (web page's '15.4 pre-outs' conflicts — treat 15.2 as right).

avpro-ac-avdm-v3.notes: Inline HDMI de-embedder; Atmos/DTS-HD → LPCM 2.0. The no-video-distribution bridge.

avpro-mxnet-1g-avdm-ev2.notes: MXNet encoder with a real Dolby/DTS → 2ch downmix on its balanced 5-pin out. HDMI loop out; Toslink OUT reserved ('future audio return support only'); no coax. 1 unbalanced 3.5mm analog in; network = 1 RJ45 PoE + 1 SFP. AUDIT 2026-09-27: was 'no toslink out' — it has one (inactive); added HDMI loop + analog in.

avpro-acp-axis2.notes: TV audio → Dante/AES67: eARC + Toslink + coax inputs (auto-switch on signal), 2 Dante channels out on 1 RJ45 (PoE 802.3af or USB-C 5V). The eARC Dante encoder (ACP-DANTE-ETV) is listed discontinued; AVPro doesn't name the AXIS2 its successor. AUDIT 2026-09-27: added optical + coax inputs. AUDIT 2026-09-27: manual — the TV MUST be set to stereo PCM output ('loud noises will ensue' with bitstream). Unicast: each channel to 2 receivers; multicast: up to 8 devices.

avpro-ac-mx-88.notes: 8x HDMI in/out (no HDBaseT outs — 'HDBaseT compatibility mode' only). AUDIO 1–8 on the rear panel: each block = 1 Toslink/SPDIF (up to 5.1 bitstream) + 1 balanced 5-pin 2ch. NO DOWNMIX (manual pp.42–43: 'this unit does NOT down mix … see AC-AXION-4') — the balanced outs only play if the source sends 2ch PCM; set Apple TV/cable boxes to stereo for zones fed this way, or use the Toslink. Extraction modes bind-to-input (default) / bind-to-output / independent matrix. AUDIT 2026-09-27: optical 4 → 8, confirmed from the manual's rear-panel drawing (p.6); downmix flag removed.

avpro-mxnet-sw12.notes: 12 ports are NOT 12 endpoint ports: 8x GbE PoE+ endpoint + 4x 10G SFP+ uplink/aggregation. SKU transitioning to AC-MXNET-SW8P — identical hardware, renamed to match the true 8-endpoint-port count. AUDIT 2026-09-27: PoE budget 125W (AVPro page + datasheet — the datasheet still carries an editor's note 'change 370W to 125W'). Plus 1 console port.

avpro-mxnet-cbox-ha.notes: MXNet control box, high-availability: 8 RJ45 LAN (one is the 802.3af PoE power port), 5-pin RS-232 (system control), RJ45 RS-232 HA heartbeat, USB-C service, optional 12V DC. HA units run in MATCHED PAIRS and don't mix with older CBOX models. TAA version is its own SKU (AC-MXNET-CBOX-HA-TAA). 10G-CBOX discontinued. AUDIT 2026-09-27: verified from the AVPro datasheet (was '6 LAN ports'). AUDIT 2026-09-27: CBOX-HA runs ONE discrete mode — 1G, USP, 10G or Dante ('only devices of that type are supported'): a 1G + 10G house needs one per platform, plus one for Dante.

ubiquiti-udm-se.notes: AUDIT 2026-09-27: 2 x 10G SFP+ (one WAN, one LAN) + 1 x 2.5G RJ45 WAN + 8 x 1G LAN.

ubiquiti-usw-pro-max-24-poe.notes: MXNet on UniFi = viable, integrator-configured, not AVPro-qualified (~9W/endpoint PoE). AUDIT 2026-09-27: 24 RJ45 TOTAL = 16 x 1G + 8 x 2.5G (was double-counted as 24 + 8).

ubiquiti-usw-pro-max-48-poe.notes: AUDIT 2026-09-27: 48 RJ45 TOTAL = 32 x 1G + 16 x 2.5G (was double-counted as 48 + 16).

audiocontrol-m4800d.notes: No RS-232. 1 local analog per zone. AUDIT 2026-09-27: Dante 16x16 on a Broadway chipset (manual); 8 stereo VIRTUAL Dante inputs per amp; more than 8 non-AudioControl Dante sources needs a controller (the Dante-mode CBOX).

audiocontrol-m6800d.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (M6400/M6800 user manual): analog inputs are per-zone stereo RCA (8 zones = 8 stereo ins) with hard-wired loop outs; the 2 bus inputs are DIGITAL (coax/Toslink selectable) — analog count corrected from 10 to 8. AUDIT 2026-09-27: Dante 16x16 CONFIRMED in the manual (tx no longer presumed); added 2 coax S/PDIF outs. 8 stereo VIRTUAL Dante inputs; internal 10x10 stereo matrix. Surround from an AXIS16 works with static routing: one zone per pair (FL/FR, SL/SR, SBL/SBR), center and LFE each on their OWN zone (mono/bridged, LFE low-pass) — never pair C with LFE (DSP/crossover are per zone).

audiocontrol-d2800.notes: LAN is control/DSP ONLY — never give it a Dante edge. AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 1 stereo Bus-B loop out (manual rear panel; AVPro's web page claims 4 local + 1 bus loop outs — conflicts, verify on a unit). Bus A is one source selectable as RCA/coax/optical.

audiocontrol-d4600.notes: AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 9 stereo RCA loop outs (8 local hard-wired + 1 Bus A).

audiocontrol-cm2-750d.notes: 750W/ch @70V — the landscape workhorse. AUDIT 2026-09-27: inputs 16 → 2 stereo (4 mono channels, each on RCA or Phoenix; the web page's '8 balanced, 8 unbalanced' is copied from the CM4). Added 2 coax outs. Zones = 1 stereo (2 mono zones in CM firmware). Per channel: 70V 750W or Lo-Z 625W; 100V is BRIDGED only (1500W).

audiocontrol-bijou-3100.notes: Compact zone amp with eARC in — a TV-return path. Outputs: 1 sub + 1 stereo pair of assignable line/preamp outs (headphone/BT-adapter downmix tap). AUDIT 2026-09-27: line outs are ONE stereo pair (assignable as surrounds/heights/headphone downmix), not 2.

audiocontrol-acp-dante-e-poe.notes: Legacy source → Dante on-ramp. AUDIT 2026-09-27: 1 stereo RCA pair (was 2); Toslink takes priority over analog — one source at a time. Ultimo-class: unicast each channel to 2 receivers, multicast to 8 — set multicast when 3+ amps subscribe.

savant-avb-output-module.notes: CORRECTED verified flag only (port count was already right). Legacy AVB backplane output card — 8 stereo pairs / 16 RCA jacks unbalanced (AOM-D16U-00, also branded AOM-016U) or 8 balanced stereo pairs on screw-down connectors (AOM-BAL16-00). Pre-amp/line level only, no on-board amplification. Card for a Savant MSC/SSP modular matrix switcher. Still fielded; NOT the current spec path — see savant-pav-aom8c. AUDIT 2026-09-27: these are cards for Savant MSC/SSP modular matrix switchers (AOM-BAL16 QRG), not an 'SVS rack chassis' AVB backplane.

savant-avb-input-module.notes: CORRECTED (was inputs: {analog:8, optical:2}, verified:false). This is the legacy AVB backplane input card — 8 unbalanced stereo RCA inputs (AIM-0A16-05, 16 RCA jacks) or 8 balanced stereo inputs (AIM-BAL16-01). PURE ANALOG — no coax, no optical, no digital of any kind; the optical:2 in the old placeholder was never real on this SKU. Card for a Savant MSC/SSP modular matrix switcher, no PoE, no standalone control ports. Still fielded in older installs; NOT what Savant sells for new AVB audio designs — see savant-pav-aim7c for the current spec path. AUDIT 2026-09-27: card for a Savant MSC/SSP modular matrix switcher (inferred from the sibling output card's QRG).

sonance-blaze-pzc-508.notes: 1U, 60W/ch @4/8Ω Lo-Z (500W total) or 125W/ch Hi-Z (70V/100V). 8 balanced Euroblock + 8 unbalanced RCA analog inputs (paired 1:1 with channels), full-matrix DSP via PowerZone Control web app. No Dante — use 1008D for that. AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones counted as STEREO zones: 4 (8/4 channels). Analog = 4 stereo sources (8/4 RCA mono + 8/4 Euroblock mono — whether RCA and Euroblock are independent sources is unconfirmed; counted conservatively). Added S/PDIF in + out (connector type unconfirmed, logged as coax). AUDIT 2026-09-27: Hi-Z is 4 x 125W (channels pair up); the 1U line has NO Lo-Z bridge mode.

sonance-blaze-pzc-1008d.notes: 1U, 125W/ch Lo-Z (1000W total) or 250W/ch Hi-Z 70V/100V. 8 balanced Euroblock + 8 unbalanced RCA analog inputs. GOTCHA: Dante is a fixed Ultimo 4x4 chip regardless of amp channel count — an 8-channel amp only gets 4 Dante channels in/out, not 8. Full-matrix DSP via PowerZone Control web app. AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones counted as STEREO zones: 4 (8/4 channels). Analog = 4 stereo sources (8/4 RCA mono + 8/4 Euroblock mono — whether RCA and Euroblock are independent sources is unconfirmed; counted conservatively). Added S/PDIF in + out (connector type unconfirmed, logged as coax). AUDIT 2026-09-27: Hi-Z is 4 x 250W (4 outputs), not per channel.

sonance-blaze-pzc-2004d.notes: 2U full-rack, 500W/ch SE or 1000W/ch bridged (BTL), 1000W @70V/100V. Dante Ultimo 4x4 chip — matches the 4 amp channels exactly here (unlike the 1008D). AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones counted as STEREO zones: 2 (8/4 channels). Analog = 2 stereo sources (8/4 RCA mono + 8/4 Euroblock mono — whether RCA and Euroblock are independent sources is unconfirmed; counted conservatively). Added S/PDIF in + out (connector type unconfirmed, logged as coax). AUDIT 2026-09-27: 500W/ch is @4Ω (250W @8Ω); 70V/100V is 2 x 1000W BRIDGED, not per channel.

sonance-blaze-pzc-6008d.notes: 2U full-rack flagship, 750W/ch SE or 1500W/ch bridged (BTL), 1200W @70V/100V. Same Dante-4x4-on-8-channel gotcha as the 1008D. 6000W total system power — verify house electrical service before spec'ing multiples. AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones counted as STEREO zones: 4 (8/4 channels). Analog = 4 stereo sources (8/4 RCA mono + 8/4 Euroblock mono — whether RCA and Euroblock are independent sources is unconfirmed; counted conservatively). Added S/PDIF in + out (connector type unconfirmed, logged as coax). AUDIT 2026-09-27: 750W is @4Ω (400W @8Ω); Hi-Z is 4 x 1200W @70V / 4 x 1500W @100V.

sonance-dsp-2-150-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 2-150 MKIII manual + datasheet): factory Hybrid Input/Output Module = 1 stereo RCA analog in + loop out + 1 coax + 1 Toslink — USE ONLY ONE INPUT TYPE at a time (selectable, not simultaneous sources). 150W/ch @8Ω, 224W @4Ω, bridged 473W. SonARC v2 DSP. Half-width 1U. AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones = 1 stereo (manual: channels as stereo pairs); added 1 unbuffered stereo RCA loop out.

sonance-dsp-8-130-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 8-130 MKIII manual): rear panel carries 4 stereo RCA analog input pairs STANDARD (1L-4L/1R-4R — all 8 channels fed as 4 stereo sources) + non-buffered loop outs. CORRECTS the distributor claim of shipping half-populated. Manual prose references coax/optical digital inputs but the rear-panel figure shows analog only — digital arrives via optional DIM/HIM modules, count unpublished. 130W/ch Class-D, stable to 2Ω, bridgeable. 1RU. AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones = 4 stereo (manual: channels as stereo pairs); added 4 unbuffered stereo RCA loop outs.

sonance-dsp-2-750-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 2-750 MKIII manual, rear-panel diagram): analog stereo in + loop out + 1 coax + 1 Toslink — 'Use Only One Type Of Input Connection'. 750W/ch @4Ω or 70V (70V is default mode), bridgeable. The landscape/garden workhorse — pairs with Sonance Garden Series (8 sats + 1 sub per amp, expandable 16+2). AUDIT 2026-09-27: zones = 1 stereo (manual: channels as stereo pairs); added 1 unbuffered stereo RCA loop out. AUDIT 2026-09-27: 500W/ch @8Ω; 750W is @4Ω/70V; bridged 2000W.

audiocontrol-acp-dante-d-poe.notes: Dante → legacy analog endpoint (the decoder counterpart to the ACP-DANTE-E-POE already in the catalog). 1x stereo RCA analog out. PoE or USB-C 5V. Configurable 1/2/5ms latency. AUDIT 2026-09-27: 1 stereo RCA pair out (was 2).

avpro-mxnet-1g-ev2.notes: Standard (non-downmixing) MXNet 1G Evolution II encoder. HDMI loop-out + balanced stereo analog de-embed (5-pin Phoenix) + Toslink. GOTCHA: Toslink is currently 'Future Audio Return Support Only' — eARC/ARC not active yet. This is a straight PCM de-embed, not a Dolby/DTS downmixer — use the AC-MXNET-1G-AVDM-EV2 (already in catalog) for Atmos/DTS-HD → 2ch. PoE 802.3af (15.4W). AUDIT 2026-09-27: added 1 unbalanced 3.5mm analog IN (embedded into the stream); network = 1 RJ45 PoE + 1 SFP. CONFLICT: the EV2 datasheet says the 5-pin out is 'downmixed to PCM 2ch' — possibly copied from the AVDM sheet; test on a unit before relying on either.

avpro-mxnet-1g-dv2.notes: Standard MXNet 1G Evolution II decoder. 1x HDMI out, balanced stereo analog de-embed, Toslink (same 'future ARC support only' caveat as the EV2 encoder — no active downmix/eARC today). PoE 802.3af (15.4W). AUDIT 2026-09-27: the decoder's Toslink is an INPUT (future audio return), not an output. Also 2 USB-A (KVM), 3 IR, RS-232; network = 1 RJ45 PoE + 1 SFP.

avpro-mxnet-sw24.notes: DISCONTINUED (AVPro Global) — replaced by AC-MXNET-SW24P (same 24x GbE PoE+ + 4x 10G SFP+). 370W PoE budget confirmed. Still fielded; for new designs spec the SW24P, or the SW24E economy variant (Layer 2.5, 4x 1G SFP stacking, also 370W). AUDIT 2026-09-27: also 4 x 1G SFP combo ports, OOB management + console + USB.

avpro-ac-mx-44.notes: 4x4, 18Gbps, dual audio de-embed per output: 4x Toslink (up to 7CH PCM/DD/DTS) + 4x balanced 5-pin analog (2CH PCM). Rear panel confirmed from AVPro cut sheet 2026-09-20: AUDIO 1-4 blocks, each TOS + L+/L-/gnd/R+/R-. Extracted audio has 3 modes: bind to input, bind to output, or independent matrix. Per-output audio delay up to 630ms. AUDIT 2026-09-27: no downmix (manual pp.40–41) — balanced outs need a 2ch PCM source; Toslink carries 5.1.

avpro-ac-mx-1616.notes: CONFIRMED (Markertek AC-MX-1616 Gen 2 spec): 16x16 HDMI 18Gbps, 16x balanced analog de-embed (5-pin terminal, ships with 16 extraction cables), 3 extraction modes (bind input / bind output / independent matrix). NO Toslink/coax digital de-embed — the distributor 'digital coax outputs' blurb was wrong. AUDIT 2026-09-27: 16 balanced 5-pin analog outs, 2ch PCM only; no Toslink/coax/HDBaseT. SKU AC-MX1616-AUHD-GEN2.

savant-pav-aim7c.notes: CURRENT Savant spec path for local-source-to-AVB-network audio input, replacing the legacy AIM-0A16 backplane card. "7 Source Audio Input IP Transmitter": 3x analog stereo RCA + 2x coax S/PDIF + 2x optical Toslink = 7 total sources, encoded and sent over a standard AVB-capable IP network (no proprietary backplane). Standalone box (PoE on -10/-20 SKUs; -00 is 5V DC), not a rack card. Also has 2x RS-232 + 6x IR control ports for source control. GOTCHA: nearly 3x fewer analog inputs than the legacy card it replaces — a straight 1:1 module swap on an existing job will likely come up short on analog sources. AUDIT 2026-09-27: the -00 SKU runs on a 5V DC 3A adapter; PoE (802.3af) is the -10/-20 SKUs only — order -10 for PoE.

savant-pav-aom8c.notes: CURRENT Savant spec path for AVB-network-to-zone audio output, replacing the legacy AOM-D16U backplane card. Marketed as "16-Channel Audio Output IP Receiver" = 8 stereo pairs, unbalanced RCA, any-stream-to-any-output routing. Receives up to 8 AVB streams from the network and can route any stream to any of the 8 stereo outputs (matrix-style, not fixed-assignment). Max 15W draw (PoE on -10 SKU; -00 is 5V DC) (fits 802.3af). Supports mute/volume/PEQ/mono-sum/up to 160ms delay per output, plus GPIO to trigger an external amp. Balanced version: see savant-pav-aombal8c. AUDIT 2026-09-27: connector is RCA only; -00 = 5V DC 3A adapter, PoE on -10 only.

savant-pav-aombal8c.notes: Balanced-output sibling of the PAV-AOM8C-00 — same 8-stereo-pair count and up-to-8-stream AVB routing, but 8 stereo pairs of balanced (Euroblock/screw-down) output instead of unbalanced RCA. Use for long commercial runs or noisy electrical environments. AUDIT 2026-09-27: 5-pin Phoenix (L-/L+/G/R-/R+) @4.2Vrms, 2 GPIO. PoE is revision-dependent (2022 QRG says yes, deployment guide omits it) — confirm; a 5V PSU ships in the box.

savant-ip-audio-125.notes: All-in-one amplified host: 4 amplified stereo zones @125W/ch (8 channels, 4-pin connectors) + 2 pre-amp zones (1 RCA + 1 Toslink out), 2 stereo RCA + 2 Toslink local inputs, built-in Savant Music 2.0 server (1 stream), Ecosystem/IP-Audio-Host licensing tier. AC powered (515W max) — no PoE. 2U. Also 6 IR, 2 RS-232, relay, GPIO. AUDIT 2026-09-27: verified from QRGs 009-1657-07 / 009-1584-01: inputs added, amp channels 4 → 8, PoE removed.

savant-ip-audio-50v2.notes: All-in-one amplified host, smaller sibling of the IP Audio 125: 4 amplified zones @50W/ch (rated, 8Ω) + 2 pre-amp zones (one RCA, one Toslink out — explicitly confirmed, not the same zone). 4 local audio inputs (2 analog + 2 digital) feeding the amp/AVB network in addition to whatever arrives over AVB. Built-in Savant Music 2.0 server. Max power draw 225W. AUDIT 2026-09-27: digital inputs are 2 TOSLINK (not coax/optical combo); 8 amp channels (4 stereo zones); AC powered, no PoE; 100Base-T Ethernet; 4 IR + 1 RS-232.

savant-pav-sms2001.notes: All-native AVB music streamer/source — 1x Ethernet port carries AVB to feed amps/AOMs directly over the network, plus 1x physical coax and 1x physical optical output for feeding a legacy (non-AVB) zone amp or AVR directly. Max 15W (PoE on -10 SKU; -00 is 5V DC). Supersedes the legacy SMS-1001/SMS-100AM single-stream servers and the older SMS-002A SmartMedia Server (500GB local storage, 2 simultaneous streams — EOL, see Unresolved). AUDIT 2026-09-27: PoE is the -10 SKU only.

sonos-amp.notes: One stereo zone, 2 amplified channels. 125W/ch RMS @8Ω (0.1% THD), roughly doubles into 4Ω (4Ω minimum load) — GOTCHA: several retailers title the SKU '250W' (125x2 summed, not per-channel); don't let that inflate a per-channel power figure in capacity math. 1x HDMI **ARC** input (not eARC) for TV sound — note the Amp is 2-channel only, so even over ARC it plays TV audio as a stereo downmix, no Atmos object/height decoding (contrast with the Arc Ultra/Beam Gen 2 soundbars below, which DO decode Atmos because they have the driver array for it). 1x stereo RCA line-in (turntable/CD), shareable/groupable to play on other Sonos rooms subject to the same 75ms line-in buffering as the Port (see headline note above). Auto-detecting sub output, adjustable 50–110Hz crossover. Dual 10/100 Ethernet (NOT gigabit — irrelevant for the Amp's own low-bitrate audio stream, but a hard ceiling if daisy-chaining other gear off it) or WiFi. Each of the 2 channels can drive 2 pairs of 8Ω speakers wired in parallel (4Ω net) — i.e. up to 4 speakers total (2 pairs) off one Amp, but they're all ONE volume zone; a second physical area needing independent volume needs its own Amp or a volume-control speaker selector downstream. NO 70V/100V capability — confirmed absent from every spec source found; Sonos amps are low-Z consumer-grade only, never spec this for a 70V distributed run. AUDIT 2026-09-27: optical in only via the Sonos Optical Audio Adapter (sold separately) on the HDMI port.

sonos-port.notes: Bidirectional bridge box, not just a one-way source: the SAME unit simultaneously (a) ingests a legacy analog source (turntable, CD player, an AVR's 2ch preout) via its 1x stereo RCA line-in and makes it available/groupable across the Sonos system, AND (b) decodes whatever the Sonos system is playing back out to a legacy zone amp/receiver via 1x stereo RCA line-out + 1x digital coax out (NO optical out — coax only). Also has a 12V trigger output (200mA) to power on a downstream amp, not counted in the port totals above. Dual 10/100 Ethernet, no PoE. LIP-SYNC GOTCHA (see headline note): minimum 75ms buffered latency on the line-in path the moment it's grouped with other rooms, by design, for multiroom sync — stacks with the TV's own ~100–150ms video-processing delay if used to encode TV audio. Sonos added Group Audio Delay + Audio Delay compensation settings in app/firmware 10.6.2 specifically for this; treat as 'viable with per-room tuning,' not 'automatically lip-synced out of the box.' No successor SKU found as of this research date — 'Port 2' appears to be unfounded/no active rumor (see Unresolved).

sonos-arc-ultra.notes: Current flagship soundbar. Single HDMI eARC port ONLY — no HDMI inputs of any kind, no analog; optical only via the separately sold adapter. Every external source must be routed through the TV and back down the single eARC connection; you cannot patch a second source directly into the bar. 9.1.4-channel driver array (up to that config with 2x Era 300 surrounds + Sub 4). Bluetooth streaming supported as a secondary input path. Pairs with Sub 4 and Era 100/300 as surrounds (see those entries) — when an Era is bonded as a surround, its own line-in is disabled (see sonos-era-300 notes). AUDIT 2026-09-27: sonos.com lists no Ethernet/USB-C port; a secondary source claims built-in Ethernet — CONFLICT, check a unit before relying on a wired drop.

sonos-beam-gen2.notes: Mid-tier soundbar. Single HDMI eARC input (backward compatible with ARC-only TVs). Ships with an optical adapter in the box for TVs with no ARC/eARC — GOTCHA: using the optical adapter drops Dolby Atmos entirely (optical can't carry the Dolby Digital Plus/TrueHD bitstream Atmos needs), falls back to 5.1/stereo. Has its own Ethernet port for wired network. 5.0.2-channel driver array; supports Atmos via HDMI eARC/ARC using Dolby Digital Plus (lossy) or, over eARC only, Dolby TrueHD (lossless). NOTE 2026-09-27: still sold alongside the Beam Ultra (sonos.com) — Gen 2 keeps the ethernet jack and the in-box optical adapter the Ultra drops.

sonos-ray.notes: Budget/entry soundbar. NO HDMI at all — optical (Toslink) digital input only, ships with the optical cable in box. No eARC/ARC means no Dolby Atmos support — format ceiling is Stereo PCM, Dolby Digital 5.1, DTS Digital Surround. Has a built-in IR receiver so the TV's own remote still controls volume/power despite no HDMI-CEC link. Has its own Ethernet port. Good fit for a secondary/bedroom TV zone where the budget doesn't support eARC gear; wrong choice anywhere Atmos or multi-source HDMI switching matters.

sonos-sub4.notes: Wireless subwoofer, no line-level or HDMI ports at all — pairs over WiFi (802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax) to an Arc Ultra/Arc/Beam or a stereo pair; has an optional 10/100 Ethernet port for a wired network connection but nothing an integrator patches into. Dual force-cancelling 5x8" woofers, ~25Hz extension, dual Class-D amps on board. Zero port-capacity relevance for the trunk checker — included here purely so the BOM/notes list doesn't have to invent a device for it.

sonos-era-300-surround.notes: Line-in requires a separately-sold USB-C adapter (Sonos Line-In Adapter: 3.5mm-to-USB-C, or the Combo Adapter which adds an Ethernet port) — there is no line-in jack on the speaker itself. GOTCHA: line-in is automatically DISABLED whenever the Era 300 is bonded as a home-theater surround speaker (paired behind an Arc/Arc Ultra/Beam) — you cannot use a surround-paired Era 300 as a line-in zone at the same time; it's one role or the other. Two Era 300s pair as rear surrounds for Atmos height content.

sonos-era-100-surround.notes: Same line-in-via-separately-sold-USB-C-adapter and same surround-disables-line-in gotcha as the Era 300 (see that entry). Smaller/cheaper stereo bookshelf speaker, used as budget surrounds behind a Beam/Ray or as standalone stereo/line-in zones where cost matters more than the 300's spatial driver array.

sonos-connect.notes: LEGACY — sold until the Port replaced it (~2019); no new features since May 2020. Gen 1 is S1-only; units built from ~early 2015 (serial date code 1502+) are S2-compatible — check the serial before planning a mixed system. Inputs: ONE analog RCA line-in. Outputs: analog RCA + Toslink optical + coax. Dual 10/100 Ethernet. Never had HDMI. Do not spec new. AUDIT 2026-09-27: verified from the Sonos CONNECT Product Guide — the old coax/optical INPUTS never existed; optical output added.

sonos-connect-amp.notes: LEGACY — sold until the Amp replaced it (~2018); no new features since May 2020. Gen 1 S1-only, Gen 2 S2-compatible (check serial). One analog RCA line-in, sub out, 55W/ch @8Ω, speaker binding posts, dual 10/100 Ethernet, no HDMI. Eligible for Sonos Trade Up. Do not spec new. AUDIT 2026-09-27: digital inputs removed (never existed).

sonos-beam-ultra.notes: Verified 2026-09-27 against sonos.com Tech Specs + Sonos newsroom. Ships 2026-09-29; Beam (Gen 2) stays on sale. 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos, 9 drivers / 9 Class-D amps (5 tweeters incl. 2 up-firing, 4 woofers). ONE HDMI eARC port (ARC fallback), no HDMI input/passthrough. GOTCHAS vs Beam Gen 2: (1) NO ethernet jack — wired network needs the Sonos Combo Adapter on USB-C (sold separately; same port takes the Line-In Adapter); (2) optical adapter NOT in the box (sold separately) and TrueHD/Atmos/multichannel PCM all need eARC — optical drops Atmos; (3) DTS Digital Surround only, no DTS:X; (4) 29.5in wide (750 mm) vs Gen 2's 25.6in — check the space under the TV; wall mount is its own part. Wi-Fi 6, BT 5.3, AirPlay 2, Sonos Voice Control (no Alexa/Google listed), far-field mics w/ hardware switch, works with the TV remote. Pairs with Sub Mini/Sub, Era 100 surrounds (Sonos Immersive Set), Ace/Ace Ultra TV audio swap. Needs the current Sonos app (Sonos 27). Control-system drivers (Savant/C4/Crestron) not yet stated for this model — confirm before quoting into an integrated job. AUDIT 2026-09-27: line-in counted (USB-C Line-In Adapter); Sonos also lists Play / Move 2 as surround options.

avpro-mxnet-sw24p.notes: Current successor to the discontinued AC-MXNET-SW24: 24x GbE PoE+ endpoint ports, 4x 10G SFP+ uplink/aggregation, 370W PoE budget. Sibling AC-MXNET-SW24E = economy Layer 2.5 variant (4x 1G SFP stacking, same 370W) for smaller deployments.

avpro-acp-axis16.notes: Hyperion Axis16 — TV eARC (or Toslink/coax; coax wins, digital overrides eARC, falls back after 10s) → up to 16 Dante/AES67 channels: 9.1.6, or up to 9.1.4 + a stereo downmix pair (UBL/UBR slots become DM-L/DM-R). DECODES Dolby Atmos / DTS-HD. On-board EQ, crossover, distance and level — the receiver's job, so a Hyperion or Director amp can run a surround room with no AVR. CEC volume pass-through, TCP control + API. 1 RJ45 Dante (PoE 802.3af in) + 1 RJ45 control; or USB-C 5V 2A. Manual/datasheet text says '10 channels'/'Axis10' in places — copy-paste from the ACP-AXIS10 sibling. Chipset/flows unpublished. Source: avproglobal.com/products/acp-axis16 + datasheet + manual (2026-09-27).

audiocontrol-hype-tetra.notes: Hyperion Tetra — 4-channel Class-H theater amp, 230W/ch @8Ω, 300W/ch @4Ω, bridges to 600W @8Ω. Inputs: 4 XLR + 4 RCA (mono, one per channel) and 4 Dante RX channels on one RJ45 (receive only); RCA thru outs pass analog only. Trigger in/out. Counted as ONE zone (one surround set, or a height layer). No IP control in the manual (the Hyperion page mentions a web GUI — conflict). 2U, 38 lb. Pair with an ACP-AXIS16 for a receiver-less theater. Source: avproglobal.com/products/acp-hype-tetra + Hepta manual.

avpro-mxnet-sw24e.notes: 24 x 1G PoE+ + 4 x 1G SFP + RJ45 console; 370W PoE (450W max draw); rated 23 endpoints + CBOX. Ships PRE-CONFIGURED for MXNet USP, 1G V1/V2 AND Dante (VLAN, QoS, IGMP — 'no additional adjustments required'); 4-switch-hop max. Economy Layer 2.5 sibling of the SW24P. The default dedicated Dante switch too. Source: AVPro datasheet (2026-09-27).

avpro-mxnet-sw48e.notes: 48 x 1G PoE+ + 6 x 1/10G SFP+; 740W PoE (850W max draw); rated 47 endpoints + CBOX. Pre-configured for MXNet USP, 1G V1/V2 and Dante; 4-switch-hop max. Source: AVPro datasheet (2026-09-27).

avpro-mxnet-dante-cbox.notes: The Dante controller = an AC-MXNET-CBOX-HA running the Dante firmware (a CBOX-HA is 'converted'; order it as a CBOX-HA if AVPro has no separate SKU on the quote). Uses Audinate's Dante API: discovers AVPro/AudioControl/third-party Dante devices, makes/breaks subscriptions from a web routing grid (Mentor), no PC running Dante Controller needed; not Dante Domain Manager. MODES ARE EXCLUSIVE — in Dante mode it manages no MXNet, so MXNet video + Dante audio = TWO CBOX-HAs. Lets the control system re-route Dante on the fly: Control4 'MXNET Dante Router' driver v103 (needs CBOX Dante fw 1.03; 2-ch virtual I/O, source selection only — volume stays on the amp driver); Savant/RTI/Crestron Home/Q-SYS/ELAN/URC listed as supported — confirm the Savant driver before quoting. 8 RJ45 (7 control/Mentor + 1 AV/network PoE-PD), RS-232, HA RJ45, USB-C; 12V or PoE, 4.5W. Source: AVPro KB 'AC-MXNET-DANTE-CBOX introduction guide' (2026-09-27).

avpro-mxnet-1g-dante-ev2.notes: MXNet 1G EVO II encoder with Dante built in (software on the main chip, 2x2 channels) — puts the source's audio on Dante (stereo; the 3.5mm analog in overrides HDMI audio). Dante rides the SAME RJ45/SFP as the video, tagged on VLAN 99 (MXNet on VLAN 100): the switch port must be a trunk, and Dante + MXNet share one MAC so they need different subnets. HDMI loop out, 5-pin balanced out (2ch PCM downmix), Toslink out (future audio return only), 1 RJ45 PoE + 1 SFP, USB-B (KVM), IR x3, RS-232; 9.7W. Managed by the 1G-mode CBOX; Dante routing via Dante Controller or the Dante-mode CBOX. Source: avproglobal.com product pages + datasheets, AVPro KB (2026-09-27).

avpro-mxnet-1g-dante-dv2.notes: MXNet 1G EVO II decoder with Dante (2x2). Its Dante is a break-out of the Dante stream carried from a DANTE-EV2 — i.e. the SOURCE's audio for whatever this TV is watching (audio follows video), NOT the TV's own app audio (Toslink in is ARC-only; no documented TV-audio→Dante path — add an AXIS2 if the client streams on the TV). Needs DANTE-EV2 encoders on the sources. Dante on VLAN 99 over the video cable (trunk port). HDMI out, 5-pin balanced out (2ch PCM), 1 RJ45 PoE + 1 SFP, 2 USB-A, IR x3, RS-232. Source: avproglobal.com product pages + datasheets, AVPro KB (2026-09-27).

avpro-mxnet-10g-tcvr.notes: MXNet 10G (SDVoE) transceiver — set as encoder or decoder by switch (factory default decoder). Video: uncompressed to 4K30 4:4:4 8-bit; 4K60 4:4:4 8-bit / 4:2:2 10-bit / 4:2:0 12-bit with light 1.3:1 compression; ~0.1ms in genlock mode, else 1–2 frames; Dolby Vision/HDR10+/HLG; scaler, multiview up to 32 windows, walls up to 8x8. HDMI passes Atmos/DTS:X; Toslink out up to DD 5.1 (no DD+/Atmos); 3-pin 2ch analog out; 3.5mm = in as encoder / out as decoder; no ARC/eARC documented. 1 x 10GBase-T RJ45 (PoE 802.3af in) OR 1 x 10G SFP+, plus 1 x 1G RJ45 (extension/control; sources PoE when the 10G link is fiber). ~9W; 12V PSU optional. Does NOT interoperate with 1G. Managed by a CBOX-HA in 10G mode (the 10G-CBOX is discontinued). Source: avproglobal.com product pages + datasheets, AVPro KB (2026-09-27).
